title: Ganesh Chaturthi: Celebrating Faith, New Beginnings and the Spirit of Togetherness
excerpt: There is something special about the arrival of Ganpati Bappa. The sound of devotional songs, the fragrance of flowers and incense, beautifully decorated homes, colourful pandals, and the joyful chant of “Ganpati Bappa Morya!” ...........

contentBlocks.text: Ganesh Chaturthi is not just a festival celebrated with rituals and decorations. It is a celebration of faith, positivity, wisdom, and new beginnings. In 2026, Ganesh Chaturthi is being celebrated on 14 September, marking the beginning of the festive period dedicated to Lord Ganesha.
The Beloved God of New Beginnings

Lord Ganesha is lovingly known by many names—Ganpati, Vighnaharta, Vinayaka, and Bappa. He is traditionally worshipped as the remover of obstacles and the symbol of wisdom and auspicious beginnings.
This is perhaps why Ganesh Chaturthi feels especially meaningful whenever we are about to start something new.
A new job.
A new business.
A new course.
A new dream.
Or simply a new chapter in life.
We often seek confidence before taking the first step. Ganesh Chaturthi reminds us to begin with faith, wisdom, and a positive heart.
More Than Just a Celebration

The beauty of Ganesh Chaturthi can be seen in the way it brings people together.
Families come together to welcome Bappa into their homes. Friends participate in celebrations. Communities decorate pandals, organize cultural activities, prepare delicious food, and join together for prayers and aarti.
And then there is the joy of modaks, one of the most loved offerings associated with Lord Ganesha. Along with modaks, devotees traditionally offer items such as durva grass, flowers, fruits, and other sacred offerings.
For children, the festival can mean excitement and decorations. For young people, it can mean music, creativity, and community celebrations. For elders, it often brings back memories of celebrations from their childhood.
Different generations may celebrate differently, but the emotion remains the same.
The Lesson Behind Ganesh Chaturthi
Perhaps one of the most beautiful aspects of Lord Ganesha is what he represents.
His large ears remind us to listen more. His wisdom encourages us to think before we act. His presence reminds us that obstacles are not always the end of the journey—they can also become opportunities to learn and grow.
In our busy lives, we often become so focused on reaching the destination that we forget to appreciate the journey.
Ganesh Chaturthi gives us a moment to pause.
To spend time with family.
To reconnect with people.
To express gratitude.
And to remind ourselves that every new beginning deserves courage and positivity.
A Celebration That Lives in Our Memories
When the celebrations eventually come to an end and Bappa leaves through visarjan, there is often a bittersweet feeling.
We say “Ganpati Bappa Morya, Pudchya Varshi Lavkar Ya!”—asking Bappa to return soon.
But the real spirit of the festival stays with us.
It stays in the memories of family gatherings, the laughter of friends, the prayers we shared, the sweets we enjoyed, and the moments when everyone came together as one.
That is the true beauty of Ganesh Chaturthi.
It is not only about welcoming Lord Ganesha into our homes. It is about welcoming wisdom, hope, positivity, and new beginnings into our lives.
Happy Ganesh Chaturthi!

May Lord Ganesha bless every home with happiness, wisdom, prosperity, and peace.
May He remove the obstacles from our path and give us the courage to keep moving forward.
And may this Ganesh Chaturthi inspire us to begin every new journey with faith, confidence, and a positive heart.
Ganpati Bappa Morya! ????✨
Wishing everyone a very Happy Ganesh Chaturthi!

excerpt: A teacher is not simply someone who stands in front of a classroom and explains a subject. A great teacher becomes a guide, a motivator, a listener, and sometimes even the person who believes in us when we have stopped believing in ourselves....

contentBlocks.text: Every year, Teachers’ Day is celebrated in India on September 5 to honour the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a renowned philosopher, educator, and former President of India. His life reflected the importance of education and the powerful role teachers play in shaping society.
More Than Just a Classroom

Think about your school or college days for a moment.
You may not remember every lesson from your textbooks. You may even forget some formulas, definitions, or dates. But you probably remember that one teacher who encouraged you before an important exam, helped you understand something difficult, or simply told you, “You can do it.”
That is the real impact of a teacher.
Teaching is not limited to completing a syllabus. Teachers help students develop confidence, discipline, curiosity, and the courage to ask questions. Their influence often continues long after a student leaves the classroom.
The Changing Role of Teachers

Education has changed dramatically over the years.
Today, students have access to online courses, videos, artificial intelligence, digital platforms, and information at their fingertips. Learning is no longer restricted to books or classrooms.
Yet, teachers remain important.
Why?
Because information can be found almost anywhere, but guidance cannot always be found so easily.
A teacher helps students understand what information matters, how to apply knowledge, how to think critically, and how to keep learning when things become difficult.
In professional education too, experienced mentors can make a significant difference by connecting classroom concepts with real-world situations and industry requirements.
A Thank You That Goes Beyond One Day

Teachers’ Day is often celebrated with cards, flowers, speeches, gifts, and cultural programmes. These moments are special, but perhaps the best gift a student can give a teacher is to use what they have learned.
Work hard.
Stay curious.
Be respectful.
Keep improving.
And when you achieve something meaningful, remember the people who helped you take the first step.
A teacher’s success is not measured only by how many students they have taught. It is also reflected in the lives those students go on to build.
Happy Teachers’ Day!

Teachers shape more than careers. They shape attitudes, dreams, confidence, and character.
On this Teachers’ Day, let us take a moment to appreciate every teacher, mentor, trainer, and educator who continues to share knowledge, encourage curiosity, and help the next generation move forward.
To every teacher who stayed after class to explain one more concept, answered one more question, or gave one more word of encouragement—thank you.
Your lessons may begin inside a classroom, but their impact can last a lifetime.
Happy Teachers’ Day!

title: Janmashtami: Celebrating the Birth of Lord Krishna with Love, Faith and Joy
excerpt: Some festivals are celebrated with rituals, while some are felt in the heart. Janmashtami is one such festival. It brings together devotion, happiness, family, music, and the beautiful stories of Lord Krishna that have been passed down through generations....

coverImage.alt: Janmashtami: Celebrating the Birth of Lord Krishna with Love, Faith and Joy - DIDM Cover Image

contentBlocks.text: Also known as Krishna Janmashtami, the festival marks the birth of Lord Krishna, who is worshipped as the eighth avatar of Lord Vishnu. It is celebrated on the eighth day of the Krishna Paksha, and the celebrations traditionally continue until midnight, the time believed to mark Krishna's birth.
The Story Behind Janmashtami

The story of Krishna's birth is one of hope in difficult times.
According to Hindu tradition, Krishna was born in Mathura to Devaki and Vasudeva when the kingdom was ruled by Kansa. A prophecy had warned Kansa that Devaki's eighth son would bring about his downfall. Driven by fear, he imprisoned Devaki and Vasudeva.
When Krishna was born at midnight, Vasudeva carried the newborn child to Gokul to keep him safe. He was later raised by Nanda and Yashoda, and the stories of his childhood became some of the most loved tales in Indian culture.
Perhaps this is one reason Janmashtami feels so special. The story reminds us that even when circumstances seem dark, hope can find a way.
A Festival Filled with Beautiful Traditions

Janmashtami is not celebrated in just one way. Every region has its own traditions, but the feeling remains the same—devotion and joy.
Homes and temples are decorated with flowers, lights, and images of Krishna. Devotees observe fasts, sing bhajans, listen to stories about Krishna's life, and wait for the midnight celebration. In many places, little footprints are drawn at the entrance of homes to symbolise baby Krishna entering the house.
Children dressed as Krishna and Radha add another layer of happiness to the festival. Their innocent smiles and playful energy often become the most memorable part of the celebration.
The Excitement of Dahi Handi

One cannot talk about Janmashtami without mentioning Dahi Handi.
Inspired by Krishna's childhood love for butter and curd, Dahi Handi involves groups forming human pyramids to reach and break a pot placed high above the ground. It is exciting to watch, but there is a deeper message behind it too.
Everyone has to depend on one another. One person alone cannot reach the pot. It takes coordination, trust, patience, and teamwork.
What Krishna Teaches Us

Beyond celebrations and traditions, Janmashtami gives us an opportunity to reflect on Krishna's teachings.
His life reminds us to face challenges with courage, perform our responsibilities sincerely, and remain calm when life does not go according to plan. His teachings continue to inspire people to choose the right path and maintain faith during difficult moments.
The Spirit of Janmashtami

At its heart, Janmashtami is a celebration of hope, love and togetherness.
It brings families closer, fills homes with happiness, and gives people a reason to pause from their busy lives and reconnect with faith and tradition.
This Janmashtami, let us celebrate not only Krishna's birth but also the values associated with his life—kindness, courage, wisdom, friendship, and compassion.
May Lord Krishna fill your life with happiness, peace, positivity, and love.
Wishing you and your family a very Happy Janmashtami!

title: Raksha Bandhan: A Celebration of the Bond That Grows Stronger with Time
excerpt: For some, it is the memory of waking up early because a sister has already started preparing the Rakhi thali. For others, it is about teasing a brother for forgetting to buy a gift. And for many people who now live away from home, Raksha Bandhan brings a little nostalgia—a reminder of childhood, family.........

coverImage.alt: Raksha Bandhan: A Celebration of the Bond That Grows Stronger with Time - DIDM Cover Image

contentBlocks.text: The festival is popularly known as Rakhi, but its meaning goes far beyond the colourful thread tied around a wrist.

Raksha means protection, and Bandhan means a bond. Together, Raksha Bandhan represents a relationship built on love, care, trust, and the promise of standing by one another.
Traditionally, a sister ties a Rakhi around her brother's wrist and prays for his happiness, success, and well-being. The brother, in return, gives her a gift and promises to support and protect her.
But if we look at Raksha Bandhan in today's world, the festival has a much wider and more beautiful meaning.
It is not just about a brother protecting his sister. It is about two people sharing a bond where both care for each other. Sometimes a sister is the one who gives strength to her brother during a difficult phase. Sometimes a brother becomes the person his sister calls when life feels overwhelming.
That is what makes Raksha Bandhan special.
It celebrates a relationship where there may be endless arguments, teasing, and disagreements, but when it really matters, siblings often stand together.
More Than Just a Thread

A Rakhi may be a small thread, but the emotions connected with it are not small at all.
For years, brothers and sisters may fight over the most ordinary things. The television remote. The last piece of chocolate. Borrowed clothes. Who gets blamed for breaking something at home.
And yet, these same people often become each other's strongest support systems.
There is something unique about a sibling relationship. Your sibling may know your most embarrassing childhood stories. They may know exactly how to annoy you. They may even be your biggest critic.
But they also know your journey.
They have seen you grow.
They remember the version of you that existed before college, careers, responsibilities, and adulthood changed everything.
That shared history creates a connection that is difficult to explain.
Raksha Bandhan gives us a reason to celebrate that connection.
The Stories and Traditions Behind Raksha Bandhan

Like many Indian festivals, Raksha Bandhan is connected with stories and traditions that have been passed from one generation to another.
One of the most popular stories associated with the festival is the bond between Lord Krishna and Draupadi.
According to a widely known tradition, Krishna injured his finger, and Draupadi immediately tore a piece of cloth from her saree to stop the bleeding. Her gesture was simple and spontaneous. She did not stop to think about what she would receive in return.
She simply helped someone she cared about.
Krishna was deeply touched by her act of kindness and promised that he would always protect her.
The story is often remembered because it reflects something important about relationships: sometimes the strongest bonds are created through small acts of care.
Another story connects Raksha Bandhan with Goddess Lakshmi and King Bali. In this tradition, Lakshmi tied a sacred thread around King Bali's wrist and accepted him as her brother.
These stories may be ancient, but the values they represent still feel relevant today—trust, loyalty, kindness, and the willingness to stand by someone.
A Festival That Brings Families Together

Raksha Bandhan is not usually celebrated with grand ceremonies or complicated rituals. Its beauty lies in the warmth of the occasion.
Families gather together. Sweets are brought home. A Rakhi thali is prepared with roli, rice, a diya, and the Rakhi.
The sister applies a tilak to her brother's forehead, performs aarti, ties the Rakhi, and prays for his happiness and well-being.
Then comes the part many siblings wait for—the gift.
For children, the excitement is often about chocolates, toys, clothes, or money. As people grow older, the gifts may change, but the excitement somehow remains.
The Real Gift of Raksha Bandhan
When we think about Raksha Bandhan, we often think about Rakhis, sweets, gifts, and celebrations. But the real gift of the festival is something deeper.
It is the reminder that we are connected to people who have shared important parts of our lives.
People who have seen us succeed and fail.
People who remember who we were before the world started expecting us to become something else.
People with whom we can argue freely because, somewhere inside, we know the relationship is stronger than the argument.
That is the beauty of the sibling bond.
It does not always look perfect.
There may be disagreements.
There may be distance.
There may be long periods without meaningful conversations.
But a relationship built over years often carries a history that cannot be replaced.
Happy Raksha Bandhan!

May this Raksha Bandhan bring warmth to your home, happiness to your family, and strength to every relationship you value.
May the sacred thread of Rakhi remind us that the best bonds are not measured by distance, gifts, or how often we speak.
They are measured by love, trust, and the simple comfort of knowing that, no matter where life takes us, there is someone who will always wish the best for us.
Wishing you and your loved ones a very Happy Raksha Bandhan!

contentBlocks.text: What Happened That Afternoon?

On the afternoon of February 14, a CRPF convoy was moving along the Jammu–Srinagar highway in Pulwama. Security personnel were travelling in buses, performing their regular duty in a region that has long faced instability.
A suicide attacker rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into one of the buses.
The explosion was devastating.
Forty CRPF jawans were martyred. Many others were injured. The Pakistan-based militant group Jaish-e-Mohammed later claimed responsibility.
For millions watching the news unfold, it didn’t feel real. It felt personal.
A Nation United in Grief
As the news spread, something powerful happened across India.
Cities fell silent. Candle marches were held. Strangers stood together, lighting diyas and holding placards. Social media filled with tributes, photographs, and heartfelt messages for the martyrs.
People from every corner of the country — regardless of language, religion, or political views — stood together. The pain was shared. The loss was collective.
For many, it was a reminder that the safety we enjoy comes at a cost — a cost paid by men and women in uniform.
The Aftermath and Rising Tensions
The Pulwama attack also changed the course of regional dynamics.
In response, India carried out airstrikes in Balakot, targeting what it described as militant camps. Tensions between India and Pakistan escalated rapidly, drawing global attention.
Diplomatic dialogues intensified. International leaders condemned terrorism and called for stability in South Asia.
Beyond headlines and political reactions, however, what remained at the core was the human cost — 40 families forever changed.
Honouring the Bravehearts
For most of the world, February 14 is associated with celebrations. In India, it also became a day of remembrance.
Every year, tributes are paid to the CRPF personnel who laid down their lives in Pulwama. Their names are spoken with pride. Their stories are shared as examples of courage and dedication.

These jawans were not just soldiers — they were sons, fathers, husbands, and friends. They served in one of the most challenging environments, knowing the risks but fulfilling their duty with unwavering commitment.
Their sacrifice reminds us that courage often walks quietly, in uniform.
Human Lessons from the Pulwama Tragedy
While the pain of that day remains, it also teaches us lasting lessons:
Unity is Our Greatest Strength
When faced with tragedy, India stood together — proving that unity is stronger than fear.
Freedom Has Protectors
The safety of millions rests on the shoulders of a few. Their sacrifice deserves respect and gratitude.
Terrorism Has No Borders
Global cooperation and collective responsibility are essential to fight extremism worldwide.
Peace is Precious
Strength is necessary, but lasting peace requires sustained dialogue, responsibility, and wisdom.
Conclusion: A Memory That Lives On
The 2019 Pulwama attack is not just a chapter in history books — it is a memory etched in the heart of the nation.
It reminds us of sacrifice. It reminds us of resilience. It reminds us that behind every uniform is a human being with dreams and loved ones waiting at home.
As we remember the martyrs, we do so not only with sorrow but with gratitude. Their bravery continues to inspire generations, urging us to value peace, unity, and national responsibility.

May their sacrifice never fade from our memory.
May their courage forever strengthen our resolve.

contentBlocks.text:
Every year, October 31 is observed as Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Jayanti, marking the birth anniversary of one of India’s most respected leaders and the driving force behind the country’s political unity. 

Popularly known as the Iron Man of India, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel played a crucial role in unifying over 560 princely states after independence — a monumental achievement that laid the foundation for a strong and integrated nation.

His leadership, foresight, and dedication continue to serve as an inspiration for generations. On this day, the Delhi Institute of Digital Marketing (DIDM) takes a moment to reflect on his extraordinary contributions to the nation and the timeless values of unity, determination, and leadership that he embodied.
A Leader Who Shaped the Nation

Born on October 31, 1875, in Nadiad, Gujarat, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel began his journey as a lawyer before entering India’s freedom struggle. 

Deeply influenced by Mahatma Gandhi’s principles, Patel became one of the most influential figures in India’s independence movement. His ability to lead with clarity and courage earned him immense respect, both among leaders and the masses.

However, his most remarkable contribution came after independence in 1947. India was then a fragmented land, divided into hundreds of princely states. 

Through his exceptional negotiation skills, diplomacy, and firm resolve, Sardar Patel managed to bring these regions together under one national flag. 

His success in creating a unified India was not only political but also symbolic — a demonstration of how vision and determination can turn challenges into milestones.
The Symbol of Unity and Strength

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s role as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India set the tone for the nation’s early governance and stability. 

His emphasis on discipline, order, and unity helped establish India’s administrative framework.

He believed that India’s strength lay in its unity and often reminded citizens that “Manpower without unity is not a strength unless it is harmonized and united properly.” This thought remains deeply relevant even today, serving as a guiding principle not only for governance but also for education, leadership, and entrepreneurship.
The Statue of Unity – A Tribute to His Legacy

In 2018, the Government of India unveiled the Statue of Unity in Gujarat as a tribute to Sardar Patel’s immense contribution to national integration. 

Standing 182 meters tall, it is the world’s tallest statue and symbolizes the unwavering strength, integrity, and vision of India’s Iron Man. The monument serves as a constant reminder of Patel’s efforts to bring together diverse communities and regions into one cohesive nation.

The Statue of Unity has also become a center for learning and inspiration — reflecting Patel’s belief in self-reliance, national pride, and collective progress. 

For students and professionals alike, it stands as a powerful reminder that leadership is not merely about authority but about responsibility and unity of purpose.
Leadership Lessons from Sardar Patel

Sardar Patel’s life offers valuable lessons that transcend time and profession. His leadership style — pragmatic, firm, and people-oriented — is as relevant today as it was during India’s formative years. Some of the key lessons modern learners and professionals can draw from his life include:
1) Decisiveness: Patel believed in acting firmly when it mattered most. In the fast-paced digital era, decision-making and adaptability remain crucial skills for success.
2) Integrity: His transparent and ethical approach to leadership made him a trusted figure. In any field, integrity continues to be the cornerstone of credibility.

3) Unity of Purpose: Patel’s greatest strength was his ability to unite diverse perspectives under a common goal. In organizations and educational environments, teamwork and collaboration lead to growth and innovation.
4) Commitment to Nation-Building: His dedication to India’s progress inspires every citizen to contribute meaningfully toward the country’s development.

At DIDM, where the focus lies on skill development and future-oriented learning, these values resonate deeply. 

The spirit of unity, responsibility, and continuous improvement forms the foundation of personal and professional success — principles Sardar Patel championed throughout his life.
Relevance of His Vision in the Modern Era

In a world increasingly connected through technology and digital platforms, Sardar Patel’s vision of unity holds even greater importance. 

Just as he brought together diverse regions to build a stronger nation, today’s generation must strive to use technology and innovation to bring people, ideas, and opportunities closer together.

The digital revolution offers vast possibilities, but it also demands collaboration, ethics, and inclusivity — qualities Patel stood for. His life reminds us that progress is sustainable only when driven by shared values and a collective sense of responsibility.
A Day to Reflect and Recommit

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Jayanti is not just a remembrance of a great leader; it is a reminder of the ideals that continue to shape India’s growth story. 

His contributions to national unity and governance remain unparalleled, and his vision continues to inspire new generations to act with courage, discipline, and integrity.

For learners, professionals, and citizens alike, this day serves as an opportunity to reflect on how each individual can contribute to strengthening the fabric of society — by promoting cooperation, empathy, and excellence in their respective fields.
Conclusion: Carrying Forward His Legacy

As India continues to evolve in an era of digital transformation, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s teachings remain a guiding light. His leadership, resilience, and commitment to unity are timeless virtues that hold lessons for every generation.
The Delhi Institute of Digital Marketing (DIDM) acknowledges this day as a moment to remember his extraordinary legacy — one that continues to inspire strength, progress, and unity in diversity.

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision built the foundation of a united nation; it is now our responsibility to carry that legacy forward through knowledge, innovation, and collaboration. 

His life reminds us that true leadership lies not in power, but in the ability to unite, empower, and serve — values that continue to define India’s journey toward a stronger, brighter future.

contentBlocks.text: Holi is a festival of colors and it is one of the most beautiful and vibrant celebrations in India that is based on the concept of victory of good over evil.
The festival is generally celebrated on the arrival of spring, and it brings the families together and binds them in unity.
The festival is beautifully described as the diversity and colorful culture of India and how it brings different hues of happiness and celebration into our lives.
At DIDM, we wish you a Happy Holi with all our hearts and may this festival bring lots of success, happiness, and new opportunities into your lives.
Holi is incomplete without colors, and like that, digital marketing is incomplete without the right marketing strategies and different advanced tools.
The Colors of Holi & Their Digital Marketing Significance
Let’s understand how the beautiful colors of Holi can relate to the colors of digital marketing with significance. How different hues of digital marketing lead towards a successful career.

Red - Red is the color of Passion & Energy, and when it comes to passion, content marketing is the right fit. A well-written blog, engaging social media posts, and storytelling talent create a lasting impact on our audiences and make our brands stand out in the market.

Blue - Blue is the color that builds trust and stability, and in digital marketing, blue is related to trust as well. SEO can build credibility for any brand digitally. By using the right optimized websites with SEO techniques, it will rank higher and ensure the user trust

Green – Growth & Prosperity Growth in marketing comes from performance and data-driven decisions. Just like green signifies renewal and prosperity, PPC (Pay-Per-Click) advertising helps businesses grow by generating leads and conversions.

Yellow - Yellow signifies positivity & creativity and you all know that creativity is the main element for engagement! Yellow represents the enthusiasm behind compelling social media marketing. In digital marketing, visually appealing content and unique campaigns attract audiences and spread brand awareness.

Orange - Orange brings enthusiasm & starts communication as this is a bright and energetic color. Effective communication with the help of email marketing and influencer collaborations helps businesses stay connected with their audience and drive engagement.

Purple - Purple color brings innovation & transformation and it is the color of innovation, much like artificial intelligence (AI) in digital marketing. From chatbots to data analysis, AI is transforming marketing strategies, enhancing user experience, and personalizing content.
DIDM Wishes You All a Very Happy Holi!
Color teaches us a lot and we should embrace these lessons and apply them into our digital marketing strategies to have a rocking journey.
If you are a student, entrepreneur, or business owner, these colors will teach you different hues of digital marketing that will help you to grow and stand out in your digital journey in the market.

DIDM encourages everyone to be creative, innovative, and fearless, and Holi is the festival that provides you these qualities. This festival teaches us to break boundaries, experiment, and enjoy the beauty of diversity, which is exactly what digital marketing is about.
This Holi, let’s paint our dreams with the colors of knowledge, success, and creativity!

Wishing you all a Happy and Prosperous Holi!

coverImage.alt: For the third time, DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! - DIDM Cover Image

contentBlocks.text: ASSOCHAM which stands for The Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India is one of the largest trade associations in India.
As you may already be aware if you have been following us for a while now, DIDM has had the honor of receiving awards from ASSOCHAM not once but twice in the past.
For the first time, DIDM received the Most Promising Brand award from ASSOCHAM, while for the second time, DIDM received the Eminent Fair Business Practices award from ASSOCHAM.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award

contentBlocks.text: Today, we are glad to announce that one more award from ASSOCHAM is headed for our award shelf on the 21st of March, 2023, and we are sincerely delighted to announce it.
There is no escaping the fact that this news is something that we cannot get our minds off of.

This is because apart from being one of the largest, ASSOCHAM is also one of the most reputable organizations in India, and receiving an award from ASSOCHAM that too for the third time is a very significant thing for the team at DIDM.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! 3rd Time

contentBlocks.text: About ASSOCHAM
ASSOCHAM was established in 1920 and is headquartered in New Delhi, India.
The organization represents the interests of more than 450,000 member companies from various sectors, including manufacturing, services, and trade.
ASSOCHAM plays an important role in promoting trade and commerce in India.
It works towards the development of the country's economy by creating a conducive business environment for Indian businesses and foreign investors.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! third Time

contentBlocks.text: The organization provides a platform for its members to interact and network with other businesses and stakeholders in the Indian economy.
ASSOCHAM is actively involved in policy advocacy and provides inputs to the government on various economic and trade-related issues.
It also organizes conferences, seminars, and other events to disseminate information and knowledge on the latest developments in various sectors of the economy.
The organization has a presence in several states across India and has regional offices in major cities such as Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, and Bengaluru.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award 2023

contentBlocks.text: Overall, ASSOCHAM plays a significant role in the development of India's economy by promoting trade and commerce and providing a voice for Indian businesses in policy matters.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! third Time

contentBlocks.text: Key Highlights of the ASSOCHAM Award Ceremony
1) The last time we attended the ASSOCHAM Award event to receive the prestigious ASSOCHAM award was on 9th of March, 2022, which means around a year back.

There was a great level of energy and enthusiasm among all the participants who attended the ASSOCHAM award event the last year, and the same level of energy and enthusiasm (even more) we got to see in this year’s ASSOCHAM award function.
2) The name of the ASSOCHAM ceremony was 9th MSMEs excellence awards and summit and the tagline was envisioning MSMEs’ for Bharat@100.

3) On March 9, 2022, the 8th MSME Excellence Awards and Summit was organized by ASSOCHAM at Taj Mahal Hotel, New Delhi to offer support to the MSME sector by providing recognition to the outstanding MSME based on their performance across different parameters.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award March 2023

contentBlocks.text: The event, a part of ASSOCHAM’s Annual Session under the central theme ‘Bharat@100: envisioning a globally competitive future’.
In continuation of their efforts to support and promote MSMEs, ASSOCHAM announced the 9th ASSOCHAM MSME Excellence Awards which were hosted on 21st March 2023 in New Delhi.
4) The event was attended by esteemed guests, two of whom were Shri Narayan Tatu Rane and Shri B.B. Swain.
Shri Narayan Tatu Rane is the Hon'ble Minister of the Ministry of MSME in the Government of India and Shri B.B. Swain is the Secretary at the Ministry of MSME, Govt. of India.
They both are highly respected in their respective fields and are committed to advancing the growth and development of micro, small, and medium enterprises in India.
5) We are receiving the award from ASSOCHAM for the third time in a row.
6) It was the Fair Business Practices award that DIDM received from ASSOCHAM.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! third Time MAR 23

contentBlocks.text: 7) The summit was a great opportunity for industry professionals to learn about the latest initiatives of the Government and share their own insights into how to create a more conducive environment for business growth.

8) The respected chief guests who attended the event were delighted to present us with the award for the third time. Shri B.B. Swain handed over the award to the co-founder of DIDM, Ms. Priyanka Singhal.
9) The summit featured key discussion areas like:
* Enabling Financial Inclusion.
* Access to easy finance.
* Developing appropriate dispute resolution mechanism.
* Significance of financing through a competitive invoice auctioning mechanism – Treds.
* Mitigating the Global slowdown impacts.
* Policy impact on technology integration.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! 3rd Time MARCH 2023

contentBlocks.text: * Technology Adoption in Small Business Value Chain.
* Catalytic effect of Digitalization.
* Leveraging Technology to Sustain.
* Building the digital transformation capacity of the entrepreneurship and innovation sector-support organizations.
* Support Growth Entrepreneurs Access-to-Markets through Business Matchmaking Intermediaries.
* Developing strategies to penetrate new markets.
* Significance of Channel collaboration and strategic alliances in distribution, logistics, and e-commerce.
Why DIDM is the only training company that has been awarded by ASSOCHAM three times?
DIDM is the only training company to receive ASSOCHAM's honor three times for a variety of reasons. And these are some of the reasons:
a) 100% Practical Training Sessions: DIDM provides the best live practical sessions on all digital marketing course topics.
b) Dedicated Placement Cell: DIDM is a well-structured Private Limited Company that has its placement cell tie-up with agencies and the corporate world across PAN India.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! 3rd Time MAR 23

contentBlocks.text: c) Educational Background: DIDM has 10+ years of experience in the field of digital marketing education and has helped lakhs of students through it.
d) Expert Trainers: DIDM has the most prominent and expert digital marketing trainers who have many years of experience in the digital marketing field.
e) 24X7 Customer Support: Any queries or issues are dealt with instantly with 24X7 dedicated DIDM customer support.
Conclusion
The fact that we have been awarded an award from an esteemed trade association such as ASSOCHAM even once is a great achievement for us, as we have mentioned previously.
Having received the ASSOCHAM award for the third time in our company's history, no one could possibly imagine how happy we are and how proud we are of what we have achieved.
The ASSOCHAM honors those businesses that conduct their business practices in a proper and ethical manner and who always put the interests of their customers before their own.

contentBlocks.alt: DIDM has won the ASSOCHAM Award! 3rd Time MAR 2023

contentBlocks.text: Right before you, we declare that we have always put our students first and have always put great emphasis on making them skilled digital marketers, and we will continue to do so in the future as well.
As a final note, we would like to thank ASSOCHAM for selecting us once again for this prestigious award.
We feel very pleased to know that we have met your expectations and we look forward to receiving many more awards from you in the near future.

contentBlocks.text: Shiva means ‘that one which is not’. Maha Shivratri means ‘The Great Night of Lord Shiva’ which is the day of overcoming darkness and ignorance in life. It is annually celebrated in the month of Phagun i.e. February-March and this auspicious day is believed to be the day when Lord Shiva got married to Goddess Parvati.
Some also believe that on this day Lord Shiva saved the world from the poison that emerged from the ocean during Samudra Manthan by drinking and storing it in his throat that turned his throat blue.
Lord Shiva is also known as Adiyogi and is believed to be the founder of Yoga and therefore, in the yogic tradition he is not considered as a God but as the first Guru.

Although Shivratri comes every 13th /14th night of each month of the Hindu calendar, Maha Shivratri is celebrated once a year. Devotees visit the nearby Shiva temple, organizes jaguars, observe fast and chant the name and mantras of Lord Shiva to seek his blessings. Many of them go on pilgrimage to Jyotirlingams.

Biologists have figured out that one of the biggest steps in the evolutionary process of any animal was the movement from a horizontal to a vertical spine after which the intelligence has happened. So, the festival of Shivratri is to make use of the natural energies to its maximum nightlong by doing proper meditation and uttering the right kind of mantras so that one can move one step closer to the Divine. Not sleeping nightlong is very important on this night i.e. one should keep the body in a vertical position. Maha Shivratri is not only of great significance for the people who are into a spiritual process but also for the people with family. It is said that any meditation done on this auspicious night is a thousand times more effective.

This day is also astrologically linked: when the sun and moon are in a particular alignment, it helps to raise the mind to a higher position. It is said that such days were pleasant for spiritual practices. According to Indian astrology, certain days and time frames are conducive for spiritual growth and meditation. Mahashivratri is one such day.
